Meta.title: Applying and benchmarking a stochastic programming-based bidding strategy for day-ahead hydropower scheduling

research_question_1.value: How does a stochastic programming-based bidding strategy perform compared to a traditional operator-determined bidding strategy in day-ahead hydropower scheduling?
research_question_1.reason: Implied in the Abstract and Introduction (Section 1), where the authors state the paper details Aneo's efforts to transition to a new stochastic programming-based method and benchmark its performance against the existing operator-determined strategy.

research_question_2.value: How does the method of generating price scenarios (ensemble forecasts vs. in-house generated) influence the performance of the stochastic bidding model?
research_question_2.reason: Implied in Section 3, where the authors state: 'we have therefore experimented with different ways of generating input to the stochastic model, in order to see how important this is as a driver of the performance of the stochastic bid model.'

hypothesis_1.value: Our hypothesis is that maintaining this profile [daily profile from ensemble forecasts] may be advantageous for the resulting bids and production schedules, specifically related to start/stop of units as well as ramping restrictions, and pressure head optimization.
hypothesis_1.reason: Explicitly stated in Section 3 (Price input and scenario generation). It is also reiterated in Section 5.6: 'This supports our initial hypothesis that the ensemble scenarios would give the best performance because they better represent the price profile.'

experiment_1.experiment_description: A rolling horizon counterfactual experiment comparing operator-determined bids (sent to the real market) with stochastic-based bids (evaluated based on realized market prices) using two different price scenario inputs (ensemble and in-house).
experiment_1.strategy: Rolling horizon comparison over consecutive two-week periods, resetting initial conditions (start reservoir levels) for the stochastic cases at the end of each two-week period.
data: Watercourse portfolio in NO3 price area (Norway) (This work)
Deterministic price and inflow forecasts (Aneo database)

experiment_2.experiment_description: Real-time testing where operators were provided with both their own generated bids and the stochastic model bids side-by-side, giving them the opportunity to choose which to submit to the market.
experiment_2.strategy: Real-time operational deployment and observation (June 2022 to March 2023).
data: Real-time market data and operator decisions (This work)

Section 5.1.value: It shows that the stochastic model with ensemble prices achieves the highest result, being 53% better than the operator-determined, followed by the model with in-house prices, which is 27% better than the operator-determined model.
Section 5.1.reason: Summarizes the main finding of the grand total analysis.

analysis_3.reason: Observing operator behavior and acceptance of the stochastic bids during real-time operations.

Section 6.value: During the real-time testing period, we observed that operators predominantly chose their own bids... operators ended up sometimes choosing the stochastic bids for the simpler systems (one-reservoir, one-plant) but almost never for the more complex cascades.
Section 6.reason: Describes the outcome of the real-time testing.
data: Real-time market data and operator decisions (This work)

interpretation_1.value: The stochastic-based models perform best overall, particularly in the first five periods, while the operator-determined bids perform better in the latter periods. The stochastic models are more willing to adjust production according to hourly price variations, leading to slightly higher start-up costs but better overall value in high-price periods.
interpretation_1.reason: Derived from Section 5.1 and 5.3, explaining the performance differences between the methods.

interpretation_2.value: Significant differences in reservoir value (and thus grand total) in certain periods are related to the water values used as boundary conditions, which are better adapted to the operator-determined method. The stochastic methods might end up at reservoir levels farther from the operator-determined levels, making the water value description less suitable.
interpretation_2.reason: Derived from Section 5.4, explaining why the stochastic models sometimes deviate significantly in reservoir value.

interpretation_3.value: The ensemble scenarios perform better because they have a smaller energy score and better represent the price profile, supporting the initial hypothesis. The deterministic forecast has a higher energy score than stochastic alternatives, indicating its accuracy is not good enough to rely on deterministic modelling alone.
interpretation_3.reason: Derived from Section 5.6, interpreting the scenario metrics and linking them to the hypothesis.

interpretation_4.value: Operators were reluctant to use the stochastic bids because they wanted control over the bids, preferred familiar methods, and found the 'top-down' generated stochastic bids hard to interpret for individual plants, especially in complex cascades.
interpretation_4.reason: Derived from Section 6, explaining the lack of adoption during real-time testing.

conclusion_1.value: The stochastic method can largely replicate the current operator-determined bidding strategy and even show better overall performance in the benchmark. However, additional work is needed before full automation, particularly in managing special constraints and boundary conditions.
conclusion_1.reason: Summarizes the answer to the first research question based on the benchmark results (Section 7).

conclusion_2.value: The authors conclude that the ensemble price scenarios yield better performance than the in-house scenarios, supporting their hypothesis that maintaining the daily price profile is advantageous for resulting bids and schedules.
conclusion_2.reason: Directly addresses the hypothesis and second research question (Section 5.6 and 7).

conclusion_3.value: Implementing a fully automated setup is difficult with tools that require extensive hands-on adaptation. Human-computer interaction and operator experience are crucial and must be incorporated into the new method for it to be successful.
conclusion_3.reason: Reflects on the practical application of the research question based on real-time testing (Section 7).

suggested_research_question_1.value: How can inflow uncertainty be effectively incorporated into the stochastic optimization model to produce more robust bids?
suggested_research_question_1.reason: The authors repeatedly state that including inflow uncertainty is the most significant improvement needed for their modelling setup.

suggested_research_question_2.value: How can the underlying watercourse models in SHOP be improved to better capture physical characteristics crucial for scheduling decisions?
suggested_research_question_2.reason: The authors note that updating watercourse models might be wiser than adding complexity through price uncertainty.

suggested_hypothesis_1.value: The authors hypothesise that including inflow uncertainty in addition to price uncertainty will lead to more robust bids and better handling of smaller reservoirs and strict restrictions.
suggested_hypothesis_1.reason: They state that for smaller reservoirs, inflow uncertainty might be more important than price uncertainty, and including it is a more important step towards automatic bidding.
